description: An introduction to the physical parts of a computer, including the system unit, CPU, motherboard, memory, ports, cables and peripheral devices.

mcq.questionText: What does the term 'computer hardware' mean?

options.text: The programs and instructions that run on a computer
The physical parts of a computer that you can touch
The data stored on a hard disk
The websites visited using a computer

mcq.explanation: Hardware refers to the tangible, physical components of a computer, unlike software which is the set of instructions.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the 'brain' of the computer?
mcq.explanation: The CPU processes instructions and controls the operations of the computer, so it is called the brain of the computer.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons?
mcq.explanation: The ALU carries out arithmetic operations such as addition and logical operations such as comparing two values.

mcq.questionText: What is the main work of the Control Unit (CU) inside the CPU?

options.text: To direct and coordinate the activities of all parts of the computer
To display pictures on the screen

mcq.explanation: The Control Unit fetches instructions and tells the other components what to do and when to do it.

mcq.questionText: The large circuit board to which all major components of the computer are connected is called the:
mcq.explanation: The motherboard is the main printed circuit board that connects the CPU, memory, and other devices together.

mcq.questionText: Which type of memory loses all its contents when the computer is switched off?
mcq.explanation: RAM is volatile memory, meaning its contents are erased when power is removed.

mcq.questionText: Which type of memory is non-volatile and usually stores the start-up instructions of a computer?
mcq.explanation: ROM keeps its contents even without power and often holds the instructions used to start the computer.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an INPUT device?
mcq.explanation: A keyboard is used to enter data and instructions into the computer, so it is an input device.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an OUTPUT device?
mcq.explanation: A printer produces a hard copy output of information, so it is an output device.

mcq.questionText: The metal or plastic box that holds the main components such as the CPU, memory and motherboard is called the:
mcq.explanation: The system unit is the case that houses the major internal hardware components of the computer.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of ports on a computer?

options.text: To connect external devices and cables to the computer
To increase the speed of the processor

mcq.explanation: Ports are the sockets on a computer used to plug in cables that connect peripheral devices.

mcq.questionText: Which port is commonly used to connect a flash disk, keyboard or mouse to a modern computer?
mcq.explanation: The USB (Universal Serial Bus) port is widely used to connect many peripheral devices to a computer.

mcq.questionText: A device that is connected to and works with the computer but is not part of the core processing is called a:
mcq.explanation: Peripheral devices such as printers, scanners and speakers are external devices that extend the computer's abilities.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly compares RAM and ROM?

options.text: Both RAM and ROM keep data permanently
RAM is temporary (volatile) while ROM is permanent (non-volatile)
RAM is permanent while ROM is temporary
Neither RAM nor ROM stores any information

mcq.explanation: RAM holds data only while the computer is on, but ROM keeps its data even after power is switched off.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the function of a cable in a computer system?

options.text: It processes instructions for the CPU
It carries power or data between devices through ports
It displays images on the screen

mcq.explanation: Cables physically link devices and carry electrical power or data signals between them.

fib.questionText: The physical parts of a computer that can be seen and touched are called computer _____.
fib.explanation: Hardware describes all the tangible components of a computer.

fib.questionText: The CPU is often called the _____ of the computer because it controls and processes everything.
fib.explanation: Like a brain, the CPU directs the operations of the whole computer.

fib.questionText: The part of the CPU that performs calculations and comparisons is the _____ Unit.
fib.explanation: The Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU) handles arithmetic and logical operations.

fib.questionText: The part of the CPU that directs and coordinates the operations of the computer is the _____ Unit.
fib.explanation: The Control Unit manages and coordinates all activities inside the computer.

fib.questionText: The main circuit board that connects all major hardware components together is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The motherboard links the CPU, memory and other devices.

fib.questionText: _____ memory is temporary and loses its contents when the computer is switched off.
fib.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile working memory.

fib.questionText: _____ is non-volatile memory that keeps its contents even after the power is turned off.
fib.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) retains data permanently.

fib.questionText: The box that holds the internal components such as the CPU and motherboard is called the _____ unit.
fib.explanation: The system unit houses the main internal hardware.

fib.questionText: A socket on the computer used to connect external devices is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Ports are the connection points for cables and peripherals.

fib.questionText: Devices such as printers, scanners and speakers that are connected to the computer are called _____ devices.
fib.explanation: Peripheral devices are external devices attached to the computer.

tf.questionText: Hardware refers to the programs and instructions that tell a computer what to do.
tf.explanation: That describes software; hardware is the physical parts you can touch.

tf.questionText: The CPU is responsible for processing instructions in the computer.
tf.explanation: The CPU carries out and controls the processing of instructions.

tf.questionText: The Control Unit is the part of the CPU that performs arithmetic operations.
tf.explanation: Arithmetic operations are done by the ALU, not the Control Unit.

tf.questionText: The motherboard connects the CPU, memory and other devices together.
tf.explanation: The motherboard is the main board linking all major components.

tf.questionText: RAM keeps its contents permanently even when the computer is switched off.
tf.explanation: RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is removed.

tf.questionText: ROM is a type of memory that does not lose its contents when the power goes off.
tf.explanation: ROM is non-volatile, so it keeps data without power.

tf.questionText: A monitor is an example of an input device.
tf.explanation: A monitor displays output, so it is an output device.

tf.questionText: A USB port can be used to connect a flash disk to the computer.
tf.explanation: USB ports are commonly used to connect flash disks and many other devices.

tf.questionText: The system unit is only used to display pictures on the screen.
tf.explanation: The system unit houses the main internal components; displaying images is the work of the monitor.

tf.questionText: Cables can be used to carry data or power between a computer and its devices.
tf.explanation: Cables connect devices and carry electrical power or data signals.

summary.correctAnswer: Hardware is the physical parts of a computer that can be seen and touched.
summary.explanation: It includes input, output, processing and storage devices.

summary.correctAnswer: Input devices, output devices, processing devices and storage devices.
summary.explanation: All computer hardware falls under these main groups.

summary.correctAnswer: The case that holds the main internal components such as the CPU, motherboard and memory.
summary.explanation: It protects and organises the internal parts.

summary.correctAnswer: The CPU processes data and controls all operations of the computer.
summary.explanation: It is called the brain of the computer.

summary.correctAnswer: The Control Unit (CU) and the Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU).
summary.explanation: The CU coordinates work and the ALU performs calculations and comparisons.

summary.correctAnswer: The main circuit board that connects all major hardware components together.
summary.explanation: It allows components like the CPU and memory to communicate.

summary.correctAnswer: Temporary (volatile) memory that loses its contents when power is switched off.
summary.explanation: It holds data and programs that are currently in use.

summary.correctAnswer: Permanent (non-volatile) memory that keeps its contents even without power.
summary.explanation: It often stores the start-up instructions of the computer.

summary.correctAnswer: Ports are sockets for connecting devices, and cables carry power or data between them.
summary.explanation: Together they link the computer to its peripheral devices.

summary.correctAnswer: External devices like printers, scanners and speakers connected to the computer.
summary.explanation: They extend the input and output abilities of the computer.

hoq.questionText: A student is typing a report and the computer suddenly switches off before saving. When it is turned on again, the unsaved work is gone but the operating system still starts normally. Which two types of memory explain this situation?

options.text: The lost work was in ROM and the start-up came from RAM
The lost work was in RAM and the start-up instructions came from ROM
Both the lost work and start-up came from RAM
Both the lost work and start-up came from ROM

hoq.explanation: Unsaved work was in volatile RAM, so it was lost, while the permanent start-up instructions are kept safely in non-volatile ROM.

hoq.questionText: A computer can receive instructions and display results, but it cannot perform any calculations or coordinate its tasks. Which single component is most likely failing?
hoq.explanation: Calculations are done by the ALU and coordination by the Control Unit, both of which are inside the CPU, so a faulty CPU explains the problem.

hoq.questionText: A teacher wants to connect a new printer, a mouse and a flash disk to one computer at the same time. What is the most important hardware feature the computer must have to do this?

options.text: Enough ports to plug in the cables of all the devices
More ROM chips on the motherboard

hoq.explanation: Each peripheral connects through a cable into a port, so the computer needs enough ports (such as USB ports) to attach all the devices.
